rationale_one_line: taste-skill is an opinionated, install-via-CLI agent skill whose whole argument is rules over vibes, so a mono-terminal canvas (matrix-green on near-black, the screen an agent actually runs in) carrying a MANIFESTO of color-burst declarations is the truest translation of the project's stance.
writing_tone_notes: Bold declarative, build-in-public, a touch defiant to match a 16-year-old vibecoder. Contractions where natural. No superlatives. Let the contrast carry the praise: slop versus taste, the statistical mean versus explicit rules, be-creative vibes versus written-down constraints. Lowercase rendering is part of the aesthetic, so copy should read well in lowercase.
do_rules: Keep the matrix-green accent scarce and deliberate, one charged line per beat, the way a terminal highlights a single token.
Let a non-text beat carry the explainer: the install command in a real terminal frame, and the color-burst flash words doing the punctuation.
Frame taste as constraints, not encouragement, which is the creator's own diagnosis of why models default to generic output.
dont_rules: No version number anywhere in copy (taste-skill is on v2; never say it).
Do not reuse the standout tokens across surfaces: 'slop' and 'statistical mean' live only in the scenes, '35k stars' and 'design sense' live only in the tweet.
No second chromatic accent, no gradients, no rounded cards. mono-terminal is square corners and one green.
